chunks: One of our companions, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) intended to marry Khadeejah bint Khuwaylid, Abu Talib came with his family and a number of Quraish, until he entered upon Waraqah ibn Nawfal, the uncle of Khadeejah. Abu Talib began with speech, saying: 'Praise is to the Lord of this House, who made us from the offspring of Ibrahim and the descendants of Ismail, and sent down to us a secure sanctuary, and made us rulers over the people, and blessed us in our land in which we are.'

Then, this son of my brother, meaning the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), is one who, when weighed against any man from Quraish, is heavier; when compared to any man, he is greater; and there is no equal for him among creation. And even if he is poor in wealth, for wealth is a flowing provision and a transient shade.

And he has desire for Khadeejah, and she has desire for him. We have come to you to propose her to you with her consent and command. The dower is upon me in my wealth, whatever you ask for, both immediate and delayed. And for him, by the Lord of this House, is a great share, a widespread religion, and a complete judgment.
Then Abu Talib fell silent, and her uncle spoke. He hesitated and was deficient in answering Abu Talib, and stuttering and confusion overtook him, and he was a man from the clergymen.

So Khadeejah said, initiating: 'O my uncle! You, even though you are more entitled to my person than I am in witnessing, you are not more entitled to me than my own self. I have married myself to you, O Muhammad, and the dower is upon me in my wealth. So command your uncle to sacrifice a she-camel, to prepare a feast with it, and enter upon your family.'
Abu Talib said: 'Bear witness upon her for accepting Muhammad, and for her guaranteeing the dower in her wealth.'

So some of Quraish said, 'O wonder! The dower is upon the women for the men?' So Abu Talib became angry with intense anger, and stood on his feet. He was one whom the men feared and whose anger was disliked.

He said: 'When they are like this son of my brother, the men are sought with the most expensive prices and the greatest dower. And when they are like you, they are not married except with the expensive dower.'
And Abu Talib sacrificed a she-camel, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered with his family.

And a man from Quraish, called Abdullah ibn Ghanam, said: 'Congratulations and welcome, O Khadeejah! The bird of fortune has flown for you in what was from you, with happiness. You married him, the best of all creation. And who among the people is like Muhammad? And the righteous heralded good news of him, Isa ibn Maryam and Musa ibn Imran.'
O nearness of the appointed time, which the Books affirmed long ago, that he is a Messenger from Al-Batha, a Guide and one who is guided.'

key_terms.أَبُو طَالِب: Abu Talib, uncle of the Prophet and leader of the Banu Hashim
key_terms.الْبَطْحَاء: Al-Batha, a plain in Mecca, often used to refer to the city
key_terms.الْمَهْر: Dower/Mahr, the gift given by the groom to the bride
key_terms.خَدِيجَةُ: Khadeejah, the first wife of the Prophet
key_terms.قُرَيْش: Quraish, the dominant tribe of Mecca
key_terms.وَرَقَةُ بْنُ نَوْفَل: Waraqah ibn Nawfal, uncle of Khadeejah

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the marriage proposal of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to Khadeejah (peace be upon her) in Shia sources?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the unique agency of Khadeejah (peace be upon her) by detailing her direct proposal to the Prophet, a departure from the customary patriarchal norms of pre-Islamic Arabia. It underscores the theological significance of the union as the beginning of the Prophet's domestic life, linking it to earlier biblical prophecies of Jesus and Moses, thereby affirming his status as the 'Seal of the Prophets' foretold in previous scriptures.
